Senses.Note: Frequent governed families include speaking, choosing, conjecturing, mistakenly citing, and missing or mishandling something. Cross-check with 'strictly do not' (切莫) and 'do not' (莫): the adverb 'urgently/strictly' (切) supplies urgency, while the following verb phrase supplies the prohibited act. No distinct noun or title use found, and no master-specific sense. Across the collected corpus the expression has 2829 exact occurrences in 339 distinct works.

Senses.Explanation: An emphatic warning governing an action or error: literally 'urgently avoid,' hence 'strictly avoid,' 'take care not to,' or 'beware of.' The object supplied by the record must be translated rather than replaced by a general spiritual warning. Daowu says, 'where knowledge does not reach, strictly avoid speaking of it' (智不到處，切忌道著); Daoqian answers a question about words that display the Way with 'strictly avoid choosing' (切忌揀擇); Tianyin tells the assembly 'strictly avoid conjecturing' (切忌卜度). Other high-seat warnings preserve concrete allusions: 'the sword has long gone; strictly avoid marking the boat' (劍去久矣，切忌刻舟), and 'if you are not a guest of the Dragon Gate, beware being branded on the forehead' (不是龍門客，切忌遭點額). Its Chan use is a direct warning embedded in interviews and public addresses, not a commentator's private aside.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Take care not to run about blindly
SearchAliases: take care not to run about blindly
Senses.Note: Yushan says this after a monk asks about being on the road without leaving home; when the monk answers with an image of walking, Yushan asks why he missed the first reply. Baichi uses the caution after an ordination-day claim of repaying debts. Xiaotang sets it beside drinking tea and eating when food comes, and Zhulang uses it in a funeral address. The line warns against a restless detour from the present point.

Senses.Explanation: The warning about running astray checks a student who tries to solve the present matter by moving elsewhere. Yushan and Baichi give it as direct answers to a road-and-home question and an ordination-day claim. Xiaotang links it with eating and drinking where one is, while Zhulang gives it as a funeral admonition.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB174.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Juelangsheng of Tianjie. In a Lantern Festival instruction, Juelang Daosheng asks what understanding and conduct must be like if they are to agree. He recalls Xuefeng's repeated visits, Changqing's hard-won recognition, and Dongshan's uncertainty about Yunyan's 'Just this is,' resolved only on seeing his reflection while crossing water. He quotes Dongshan's warning against seeking from another as one instance of a thorough change that lets a person act for himself. Juelang then says that gaining an entry is insufficient if one cannot break out of its habitual enclosure: earlier teachers pressed people both into entry and out into freedom, so they would neither deceive nor be deceived. The quoted pair is Dongshan's voice; Juelang's present instruction makes it part of demanding work and renewed freedom, rather than a reason to dispense with teachers or effort.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB197.xml). Essentials of the Recorded Sayings of Master Wu Yi of Boshan. A monk asks Wuyi Yuanlai about the earlier saying that recognition through conditions is quick but settling into the substance gains strength slowly. Wuyi answers with an old mirror needing no further polishing and its brightness remaining as before, then unsettles the monk's additional claims with images of a three-year-old with snow-white hair and a painted landscape that has color from afar but no sound up close. After the monk bows, Wuyi quotes Dongshan's opening pair, saying that the old man's sandals have broken and his heels are exposed. He calls his own course the same road with different tracks: whether the audience approaches from the principal or the secondary position, he will not remain stationed there. His final warning that even these words are entanglement asks them to break through his explanation too. Dongshan remains the quoted speaker; Wuyi applies the warning against seeking from another while actively refusing a settled position for the hearers to borrow.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB298.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shenfeng Xian. Shenfeng Xian recalls Dongshan seeing his reflection and quotes the poem through 'everywhere I meet the other.' He places this beside a monk asking Shishuang about brushing away dust to see Buddha, answered with 'He has no country; where would you meet him?' Shenfeng asks his assembly whether meeting everywhere and having nowhere to meet are the same or different. His verse says that sameness would be wholly sameness and difference wholly difference, warning against adding feet to a snake or trying to establish a turtle by turning it into a soft-shelled turtle. He flicks his whisk and ends the address. The old Dongshan pair remains a quotation within this present comparison. Shenfeng does not explain away either saying to give the audience a single geographical or abstract place to seek.

When the monk asks for a sentence that is neither empty nor solid, Yuansou answers with Dongshan's opening couplet. Raising his staff, he says that saving old Lu loses Shaolin's teeth. The inherited warning now serves as Yuansou's own present reply to a question built from paired categories. His actions and further criticism prevent the reader from treating the couplet as merely a third verbal category alongside the first two.

Linquan Conglun examines a monk's question to Guangde about finding subtlety amid waves. Guangde answers that no oar is used, the bottom has fallen out, and coming and going borrow no floating bag. Linquan describes the mind's vast source and the winds of action stirring consciousness, then asks whether Guangde is answering, explaining, speaking beyond convention or discussing the matter directly. He quotes Dongshan's whole reflection verse and asks whether Dongshan's awakening on crossing water was not precisely finding subtlety amid waves. Why, he asks, would such a person need a flotation device to cross? Dongshan remains the exact quoted poem speaker. Linquan's present application joins the literal crossing scene to Guangde's boat image, while still asking readers to judge how the answer works rather than supplying an ordinary method of navigation.

Senses.Explanation: Dongshan warns against seeking from another after seeing his reflection; later teachers put the warning to work in distinct questions and instructions. In a Lantern Festival instruction, Juelang Daosheng asks what understanding and conduct must be like if they are to agree. He recalls Xuefeng's repeated visits, Changqing's hard-won recognition, and Dongshan's uncertainty about Yunyan's 'Just this is,' resolved only on seeing his reflection while crossing water. He quotes Dongshan's warning against seeking from another as one instance of a thorough change that lets a person act for himself. Juelang then says that gaining an entry is insufficient if one cannot break out of its habitual enclosure: earlier teachers pressed people both into entry and out into freedom, so they would neither deceive nor be deceived. The quoted pair is Dongshan's voice; Juelang's present instruction makes it part of demanding work and renewed freedom, rather than a reason to dispense with teachers or effort. A monk asks Wuyi Yuanlai about the earlier saying that recognition through conditions is quick but settling into the substance gains strength slowly. Wuyi answers with an old mirror needing no further polishing and its brightness remaining as before, then unsettles the monk's additional claims with images of a three-year-old with snow-white hair and a painted landscape that has color from afar but no sound up close. He calls his own course the same road with different tracks: whether the audience approaches from the principal or the secondary position, he will not remain stationed there. Hengxiulin Falin owns the retained deployment: raising the birthday case with Yunmen's killing-line and Langye's verdict-cap and his too-late-drawing-the-bow — then grading both elders as very much pouring oil to save the fire, and ruling in his own name: Luluo is otherwise — let them bow to hemp-three-catties; I but namo to the dried-shit-brick; same as the men of old, or different?.

Senses.Explanation: Offer this deep mind to the dust-grain realms — that is repaying the buddha's kindness. The couplet is Ananda's own vow from the Śūraṅgama — and the Chan hall's use of it begins with a killing. The newborn World-Honored One takes seven steps, eyes sweeping the four quarters, heaven-above earth-below I-alone-venerable; Xuedou would tip over the Chan seat; Fayan grants the momentum but denies the buddha-dharma in it; and Langye Huijue caps the whole exchange where it stands: Yunmen's if-I-had-been-there, one blow to kill him and feed him to the dog, buying the world its peace — that, says Langye, may truly be called offering this deep mind to the dust-grain realms, that alone is repaying the buddha's kindness. Baiyun Shouduan lifts the couplet in the hall and turns it down the mountain: the old worthy said it — offer this deep mind, repay the buddha's kindness; Yuantong is otherwise: just now and then boil the wild greens with their roots, gather the raw firewood with its leaves still on — Go! Pu'an Yinsu sets it at the head of a stone stupa built for his parents: father passed into quiescence and that is joy, mother birthed the dharma and that is the unborn, the brothers' ten-thousand deeds grown round and bright, the nine clans' spirit-traces all holding awareness — right at such a time, offer this deep mind to the dust-grain realms, that alone is repaying the buddha's kindness. Wuyi Yuanlai moves the repayment before anything to repay: to read the Treasury of the True Eye one must meet it where the World-Honored One has not yet twirled the flower and Mahakasyapa has not yet smiled; to settle the mind one must meet it where Bodhidharma has not yet opened his mouth and the Second Patriarch has not yet cut off his arm — catch it at that season and you are still a little ahead; wait for the World-Honored One to be born, point at heaven and earth, walk his seven steps and say heaven-above earth-below I-alone-venerable, and the defeat is already conceded; so Yunmen's one blow, feeding him to the dog, buying the great peace — that may be called the repayment-vow; brothers, is there one among you who knows the kindness and repays it? If there is, let him come out and meet me. Hanxiu Ruqian, entering a new monastery, carries it hall to hall — at the Maitreya hall teasing the fat brother who cannot dodge him on the narrow road, and at the Buddha hall: the word buddha, I do not like to hear it; water does not wash water, gold does not trade for gold — the new elder is otherwise: offer this deep mind to the dust-grain realms, that alone is repaying the buddha's kindness — and bows. And Hengxiulin Falin, raising the birthday case with Langye's cap and his too-late-drawing-the-bow, grades both elders as pouring oil on the fire — and Luluo is otherwise: let them bow to hemp-three-catties; I but namo to the dried-shit-brick. Same or different from the men of old?

Entries.SourceTerm: 將此身心奉塵剎，是則名為報佛恩

Senses.PreferredTarget: Offer this body and mind to the worlds of dust; that is how to repay the Buddha's kindness
AlternateTargets: Dedicate body and mind to the countless realms; thus the Buddha's kindness is repaid
SearchAliases: body and mind repay Buddha kindness
offer body mind to dust realms
Senses.Note: The Surangama Sutra's Ananda verse reads 'deep mind' in the first clause; these six exact recorded-sayings witnesses instead say 'body and mind.' Tianyin, Tian'an, Yinyuan, Tianran, Poshan, and Linye all voice the latter form in their own present address, often as a closing answer to how one repays kindness. The substitution gives bodily conduct a place alongside intention. The earlier scriptural wording is an important related source, not an exact witness to this headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 卓拄杖。住歸宗，上堂。「剎竿依舊，毒鼓從新。祖令親行，魔外潛息。然燈身前，不容擬議。迦葉門下，許有激揚。一句根由，當眾決擇。」問荅畢，云：「天清地寧，江深嶽峙。風動雲起，晝朗夜昏。聖主垂衣，良臣補袞。四民浩浩，百氏騰騰。現成公案，還有指示也無？若無指示，老僧堪作甚麼？若有指示，大眾何曾具足？所以，遇賤即貴，寶几珍御豈是元無？遇貴即賤，白牯狸奴應非別有。揖搦並用，貴在當機。從上真宗祇言仍舊，恁麼也不得，不恁麼也不得，恁麼不恁麼總不得。石頭極口在仍舊上，猶為指蹤極則之談。我有時教伊揚眉瞬目，有時不教伊揚眉瞬目，有時道揚眉瞬目者是，揚眉瞬目者不是。馬祖用盡氣力，亦不過在仍舊上虛縱虛奪。臨濟得大愚點破，始解未到黃檗時消息。俱胝得天龍一指，受用平生，末後在童子指頭上施全殺手段、顯全活風猷，亦不過在仍舊上善為去就。始知直下承當，錯過不少；翻身跳出，轉見無端。直饒三頭八臂、鼻直眉橫，到者裏總要喫歸宗痛棒始得。且道歸宗又作麼生？」卓拄杖，云：「將此身心奉塵剎，是則名為報佛恩。」下座。上堂。「正月已過，二月初來，諸人箇箇委悉，惟有拄杖子總沒分曉。且道：委悉底是？沒分曉底是？全是？全不是？」卓拄杖，云：「道士帔白襴，知非真措大。」上堂。舉：「破灶墮云：『鏡凹照人瘦，鏡凸照人肥，不如打破鏡，還我舊面皮。』」師云：「大眾！如何是鏡現山河大地者？如何是人山河大地？且道鏡作麼生打破？面皮作麼生還舊？」卓拄杖一下，云：「會麼？霜天月落夜將半，誰共澄潭照影寒？」上堂。「歸宗斬蛇，若作舉鋤下鋤會，大似釘樁搖櫓。若作一斬兩斷會，大似劈破虛空。不可但道箇南斗七北斗八便當得。既當不得，合作麼生？」上堂。「文殊三處過夏，有一句子要人信；迦葉欲行正令，有一句子要人疑。疑句即信句，信句即疑句，疑信裏錯過，疑信裏薦取。呵呵呵！日出眾峰青，雲深不知處。」上堂。「端陽到來了，文殊、普賢、觀音在拄杖頭諍論佛法，各持一說，如鬥快龍舟相似。汝諸人為老僧捉下，有功者賞，有過者誅。咦！總是有過，且作麼生誅？」喝一喝，云：「狗銜赦書，諸侯避路。」上堂。「譬如明鏡現眾色像，像不入鏡裏，鏡不到像邊，而森羅宛然，空明自爾。到者裏，須知數點平田白，千株東嶺青，豈不是諸人分上？黃鶴樓詩猶未輪到你題在。」上堂。舉百丈野狐因緣，師云：「不落天上月，不昧庭

Entries.SourceTerm: 將謂吾孤負汝，卻是汝孤負吾

Senses.PreferredTarget: I thought I had let you down, but it is you who have let me down
SearchAliases: i thought i had let you down, but it is you who have let me down
Senses.Note: Nanyang Huizhong calls his attendant three times, and the attendant answers each call. Nanyang then says, “I thought I had let you down, but it is you who have let me down.” Sanyi quotes the exchange and questions explanations that make either the attendant simply successful or both parties simply mistaken. Nanming’s verse treats the repeated calls as a test. Guantao voices the same line when a monk leaves before answering his festival question, making it a current reply rather than a mere citation. Hanxiu asks where the attendant’s failure lies and answers with an image of a missing true listener. The ordinary words of disappointment turn the visible exchange into a question about meeting what was asked.

Entries.SourceTerm: 將謂吾孤負汝，誰知汝孤負吾

Senses.PreferredTarget: I thought I had failed you; who knew you had failed me?
AlternateTargets: I supposed I had let you down, but it is you who have let me down.
SearchAliases: national teacher three calls failed you
thought I failed you you failed me
Senses.Note: Nanyang Huizhong calls his attendant three times, receives three replies, and says this pair. Hansong doubts both sides and gives a verse; Dounan asks what the saying means; Yuejiang places the failure in calling and responding; Gulin says the case strikes like thunder. Tianan independently revoices it in a funeral address and then questions whether its tenderness goes far enough.

Occurrences.Kwic: 春雨一聲鳩。聲聲暗寫春情甚，誰識春情寄壟頭。賓頭盧尊者，因阿育王內宮齋三萬大阿羅漢。二尊者！若不是育王，並須出國。相逢便問家山路，笑指家山路不遙。回首暮雲歸未合，抬眸新月上林梢。善慧大士，一日披衲頂冠靸履，朝見梁武帝帝國。要識三教聖人體麼，恁麼也不得，不恁麼也不得，恁麼不恁麼總不得。要識三教聖人用麼，恁麼也得，不恁麼也得，恁麼不恁麼總得。直饒會得體用，拄杖猶未放過。非禪非道亦非儒，三不完全總是孤。只道聚沙終作塔，那知捏土不成珠。寶誌公垂語曰：「終日拈香擇火，不知身是道場。」善權者裏終日拈香擇火，不得喚作拈香擇火。野老家風迥異常，太平勳業總相忘。皇風一片知何處，燕舞鶯啼日正長。三祖《信心銘》曰：「至道無難，惟嫌揀擇。」大小祖師，祇會抱不哭孩兒，打淨潔地上毬子。既是至道無難，亦不礙揀擇。春暖山自青，谿晴水自綠。菜花一片金，麥浪千層碧。明不明，擇不擇，二水中分白鷺洲，風光兩岸生涯別。南陽忠國師一日喚侍者，者應諾，如是三喚三應，師云：「將謂吾孤負汝，誰知汝孤負吾。」三喚三應，缽盂安柄。兩箇郎當，一場氣悶。是則是，不圖打草，只要驚蛇。子規枝上語聲聲，暗把愁腸訴與人。啼得血流無用處，不如滅口過殘春。有婆子供養一菴主二十年，常令二八女子給侍。婆子者，僧彼此不無長處。若是佛法，三生六十劫。梅雪爭春未肯降，騷人閣筆費評章。梅須遜雪三分白，雪卻輸梅一段香。青原思禪師參六祖，問：「當何所務，不落階級？」洗耳谿邊，飲牛流上，未是老成高蹈。掃除朕蹟，撥轉機輪，試看俊俏生涯。當時纔見祖云：「落何階級？」便與掀倒禪床，豈不俊哉？背手掀翻寶座平，任從金殿五雲生。巍巍頂相難攀仰，千嶂惟餘一月明。馬祖一禪師因僧問：「為甚麼說即心即佛？」祖曰。喚鐘作甕，指鹿為馬，大師固已不能逃其責。若夫體會大道，直饒千佛出來，亦無啟口處。人間四月芳菲盡，山寺桃花始盛開。莫謂春歸無覓處，依然轉入此中來。藥山儼禪師因僧問：「如何是道中至寶？」山云：「莫諂曲。」僧云：「不諂曲時如何？」山云：「傾國不換。」貧而無諂，富而無驕，藥山老人聊亦可矣。若是道中至寶，猶未得在，何故？未若貧而樂，富而好禮者也。門外百千竿綠竹，庭前三兩樹梅花。客來莫道貧無待，清淡門牆有幾家。藥山久不陞座，院主白云：「大眾久思法誨。」藥山不惜一詞，足可觀光。及被院主

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 春雨一聲鳩。聲聲暗寫春情甚，誰識春情寄壟頭。賓頭盧尊者，因阿育王內宮齋三萬大阿羅漢。二尊者！若不是育王，並須出國。相逢便問家山路，笑指家山路不遙。回首暮雲歸未合，抬眸新月上林梢。善慧大士，一日披衲頂冠靸履，朝見梁武帝帝國。要識三教聖人體麼，恁麼也不得，不恁麼也不得，恁麼不恁麼總不得。要識三教聖人用麼，恁麼也得，不恁麼也得，恁麼不恁麼總得。直饒會得體用，拄杖猶未放過。非禪非道亦非儒，三不完全總是孤。只道聚沙終作塔，那知捏土不成珠。寶誌公垂語曰：「終日拈香擇火，不知身是道場。」善權者裏終日拈香擇火，不得喚作拈香擇火。野老家風迥異常，太平勳業總相忘。皇風一片知何處，燕舞鶯啼日正長。三祖《信心銘》曰：「至道無難，惟嫌揀擇。」大小祖師，祇會抱不哭孩兒，打淨潔地上毬子。既是至道無難，亦不礙揀擇。春暖山自青，谿晴水自綠。菜花一片金，麥浪千層碧。明不明，擇不擇，二水中分白鷺洲，風光兩岸生涯別。南陽忠國師一日喚侍者，者應諾，如是三喚三應，師云：「將謂吾孤負汝，誰知汝孤負吾。」三喚三應，缽盂安柄。兩箇郎當，一場氣悶。是則是，不圖打草，只要驚蛇。子規枝上語聲聲，暗把愁腸訴與人。啼得血流無用處，不如滅口過殘春。有婆子供養一菴主二十年，常令二八女子給侍。婆子者，僧彼此不無長處。若是佛法，三生六十劫。梅雪爭春未肯降，騷人閣筆費評章。梅須遜雪三分白，雪卻輸梅一段香。青原思禪師參六祖，問：「當何所務，不落階級？」洗耳谿邊，飲牛流上，未是老成高蹈。掃除朕蹟，撥轉機輪，試看俊俏生涯。當時纔見祖云：「落何階級？」便與掀倒禪床，豈不俊哉？背手掀翻寶座平，任從金殿五雲生。巍巍頂相難攀仰，千嶂惟餘一月明。馬祖一禪師因僧問：「為甚麼說即心即佛？」祖曰。喚鐘作甕，指鹿為馬，大師固已不能逃其責。若夫體會大道，直饒千佛出來，亦無啟口處。人間四月芳菲盡，山寺桃花始盛開。莫謂春歸無覓處，依然轉入此中來。藥山儼禪師因僧問：「如何是道中至寶？」山云：「莫諂曲。」僧云：「不諂曲時如何？」山云：「傾國不換。」貧而無諂，富而無驕，藥山老人聊亦可矣。若是道中至寶，猶未得在，何故？未若貧而樂，富而好禮者也。門外百千竿綠竹，庭前三兩樹梅花。客來莫道貧無待，清淡門牆有幾家。藥山久不陞座，院主白云：「大眾久思法誨。」藥山不惜一詞，足可觀光。及被院主

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 將謂吾孤負汝，誰知汝孤負吾

Senses.Explanation: A speaker reverses the expected blame after an exchange with an attendant. In the inherited case, Huizhong repeatedly calls his attendant and then speaks the pair. Later commentators locate the apparent failure differently, while Tianan applies the line anew in a funeral address.

Entries.SourceTerm: 將謂吾辜負汝，卻是汝辜負吾

Senses.PreferredTarget: I thought I had failed you, but you have failed me
SearchAliases: i thought i had failed you, but you have failed me
Senses.Note: Nanyang Huizhong calls his attendant three times, and the attendant answers each time. The teacher then says he had thought he failed the attendant, but the attendant failed him. Wuyi cautions against treating this as simple recognition of a voice. Yun’e asks where either side’s failure lies; Eryin speaks of the teacher’s open-hearted calling and the attendant’s exposed answer. Linwo refuses easy judgments on either side and ends with a whisk gesture. The line turns the listener back to what happened in the calls and responses.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB422.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linwo. Linwo quotes Nanyang, rejects two conventional verdicts, and offers a whisk gesture.

Senses.Explanation: Nanyang’s reversal after calling his attendant three times becomes a case about whether a response actually meets a call. Wuyi and Yun’e press the difference between merely hearing an answer and meeting what the repeated calls demand. Eryin reads both sides as exposed in the exchange, while Linwo rejects ready verdicts about which party failed.

Senses.PreferredTarget: I thought so, I thought so; so this is it, so this is it.
AlternateTargets: I expected one thing; now I see how it really stands.
SearchAliases: I thought so now I see how it is Chan
so this is how it turns out Zen
Senses.Note: Poshan laughs and says it after a charged exchange with an official. Buyan, Minshu, and Yushan say it when a visitor answer or hesitation reveals what is there; Pufu supplies it as his own alternative to an older case. The doubled words make the change of stance audible, moving from what seemed to be the case to what has become evident.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1397.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xueyan Zuqin. Xueyan welcomes the imagined challenge with a knee-strike and claims he had thought no one could attest it.

Senses.Explanation: ‘I thought there was no one’: a pointed Chan exclamation when a speaker finds, or challenges others to produce, someone able to answer. The words can stand alone or lead into a specified witness, knowing listener or buyer. Miaoyun Zhenxiong answers an elder's testing question about mill work with ‘I thought there was no one to attest it,’ and receives a slap. Xutang Zhiyu imagines someone questioning his new hall and says he had thought there was no knowing listener. Baichi Xingyuan laughs at an imagined monk who calls him skillful and answers with the short exclamation. After commenting on the old Taishan woman case, Sanshan Denglai pauses and says only ‘I thought there was no one.’ Baiyu Jingsi describes his teacher's jewel as seemingly without anyone to pay its price, then says a transmission was entrusted after all. Hansong Zhicao uses the expanded line in a remembered exchange with his elder after testing an assembly with a bamboo strip. Xueyan Zuqin strikes his knee and says it after imagining someone objecting to his own reading of Zhaozhou's four Buddhas.

Occurrences.Kwic: ，鑿山透海遵神禹，鍊石補天羨女媧。雪峰問德山：「從上宗乘，學人還有分也無？」山棒曰：「道甚麼？」峰云：「不會。」明日復請益。德山道無，固是憐兒不覺醜。丹霞道有，也只具得一隻眼。善權又不然，我宗離背觸，不立有無機。直下超凡聖，烏雞雪上啼。翠擁青山夾晝新，一般蓬戶兩般春。相知不在梨花白，縱是清茶也醉人。雪峰示眾：「世界闊一丈，古鏡闊一丈。」玄沙指火爐曰：「闊多少？」峰云：「如古鏡闊。」曰：「老漢腳跟未點地在。」玄沙者漢，慣得其便，大似家富兒嬌。正眼看來，古佛家風，又豈止掃地而已。將謂猴白，更有猴黑。展演跨灶，神出鬼沒。鏡闊火爐，大機圓應。腳未點地，大用直截。好看新月上江皋，莫認波濤翻夜雪。雪峰問僧：「甚處來？」曰：「浙中來。」至焚香禮拜。船來陸來，事絕安排，不涉不隔，語繫驢橛。兩度棒出，知恩有日，焚香悲鳴，未必好心。咄！是何言歟？關鎖重重客路岐，徒將雙足刖天涯。爭如獨巫空山裏，花落花開自有時。雪峰問僧：「闍黎名甚麼？」曰：「玄機。」峰云：「日織多少？」曰：「寸絲不挂。」峰云：「參堂去。」僧去三五步，峰云：「袈裟落地也。」僧回首，峰便打。文彩縱橫，機梭不挂。道無橫徑，理
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB392.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hansong Cao. Hansong Zhicao uses the pair while commenting on Xuefeng's saying that the ancient mirror is as broad as the world. Xuansha points to the stove and asks its width; Xuefeng says it is as broad as the ancient mirror, and Xuansha says the old man's heels have not touched the ground. Hansong remarks on Xuansha's ease but then refuses to reduce the ancient teachers' style to sweeping away another's position. After the monkey line he praises both the mirror-and-stove's rounded responsiveness and the heels remark's direct action, warning not to mistake waves for night snow. The cap opens a further dimension instead of simply declaring Xuansha the winner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 寒泉時如何？州云：苦。云：飲者如何？州云：死。雪峯聞舉云：趙州古佛從此不答話。雪竇云：眾中總道雪峰不出者僧問頭，所以趙州不肯。如斯話會，深屈古人。雪竇即不然，斬釘截鐵，本分宗師；就下平高，難為作者。師云：是則草偃風行，不是則𦘕蛇添足。山僧道：雪峰、趙州總被者僧穿却了也。何以見得？雪峰從此不答話。舉僧問西堂和尚：有問有答，賓主歷然，無問無答時如何？堂云：怕爛却去那？僧問長慶：有問有答，賓主歷然，無問無答時如何？慶云：相逢盡道休官去，林下何曾見一人？雪竇云：何不與本分草料？師云：將謂猴白，更有猴黑。忽有問：山僧有問有答，賓主歷然。無問無答時如何？只向道：一抽三，二添四。畢竟如何？高祖殿前樊噲怒。舉：臨濟示眾云：我於先師處三度喫六十棒，如蒿枝拂相似。如今思一頓喫，誰為下手？僧出眾云：某甲下手。濟拈棒與僧，僧擬接，濟便打。雪竇云：臨濟放處較危，収來太速。師云：宗師一等提持，如壯士展臂不借他力，若仔細檢點將來，未免有得有失。當時者僧待他拈棒拂袖便行，直教者漢掣電之機一點也用不著。雪竇云：臨濟放處較危，収來太速，喫得棒也未？舉：欽山一日上堂，竪起拳，又開云：開即為掌，五指參差
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1412.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Gulin Qingmao. Gulin Qingmao raises two replies to the question of what happens when there is neither question nor answer, so guest and host are no longer visibly distinguished. Xitang asks whether it will rot; Changqing says that everyone speaks of retirement but no one is seen in the woods. After Xuedou asks why not give the questioner his proper fodder, Gulin caps the series with the monkey pair. He then proposes his own response, 'Draw one, three; add two, four,' and ends with Fan Kuai's anger before the imperial hall. The old appraisals do not exhaust the matter; Gulin adds another encounter rather than explaining the monkey as a fixed symbol.

Occurrences.Kwic: 掩室而坐。頌云：白夏時將至，垂慈勉進修。人天不敬仰，歲月自遷流。法法無生滅，頭頭有放收。九旬聊掩室，恩大實難酬。結夏，上堂。雲門云：今月十五入夏也，寒山子作麼生？靈巖道：今月十五入夏也，黑漆桶作麼生？旃檀叢林，旃檀圍繞；師子叢林，師子圍繞。衲僧鼻孔大頭垂，金剛腦後三斤鐵。上堂。空生大覺中，如海一漚發。有漏微塵國，皆依空所生。國土依空生，空依大覺生。大覺無所依，是謂光明藏。眾中忽有道：依文解義，座主家風。東搭西兜，時流趣向。衲僧門下，未見作家。山僧聞與麼道，直得倒頭禮拜。何也？將謂猴白，更有猴黑。啟建聖節，上堂。拈拄杖：崇高不極，廣博無涯。是謂聖中之聖，天中之天。馭三光以照臨，總萬㝢而光宅。無思不服，有感必通。畫拄杖：擘開華嶽連天秀，放出黃河徹底清。上堂：相逢不拈出，舉意便知有。颺下柴爿，賣弄不少。罰錢出院，力盡烏江。山上有鯉魚，井底有蓬塵。千年桃核裏，覓甚舊時仁。上堂：大眾，業不可為，業不可避。不見道，假使百千劫，所作業不忘。世尊有金鎗馬麥之報，迦葉有世世金色之報。只此二報，無起相，無滅相，如風吹水，自然成文。滿，散。上堂：一年三百六十日，惟有此日最吉祥。黃河澄清
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1416.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shuzhong Wuyun. Shuzhong Wuyun first expounds a chain in which worlds depend on space, space on great awakening, and great awakening on nothing. He imagines someone accusing this of a lecturer's word-bound explanations and fashionable patchwork, lacking the workmanship of a Chan adept. Shuzhong says that hearing such criticism he would bow down, then gives the monkey pair. The critic is imagined within his present address, not a separately recorded interlocutor. His response admits a further turn upon his own exposition instead of leaving its luminous explanation untouched.

He imagines someone accusing this of a lecturer's word-bound explanations and fashionable patchwork, lacking the workmanship of a Chan adept. Shuzhong says that hearing such criticism he would bow down, then gives the monkey pair. The critic is imagined within his present address, not a separately recorded interlocutor. His response admits a further turn upon his own exposition instead of leaving its luminous explanation untouched.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 將謂鬍鬚赤，更有赤鬚鬍

Senses.Explanation: A familiar quip turns an expectation about a red beard into recognition of a surprising person. Tianran says it after lifting a staff; Baishan gives it to a monk whose answer turns the exchange. Huijue speaks it after striking his staff, while Wuyi names an older exchange and asks his own assembly whether they have a monk to match it.

Senses.PreferredTarget: to go along with the mistake
AlternateTargets: to carry the mistake forward
to proceed on the mistaken basis
Senses.Note: The phrase means proceeding on the basis of a mistake already in play. Context decides whether that continuation is expedient, constrained, or condemned; those stances do not create separate senses.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB205.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jieweizhou: Jieweizhou first quotes Muyun Tongmen's letter, then rejects carrying a faulty account forward under that excuse; the second headword occurrence is Jieweizhou's own voice.

Senses.Explanation: To go along with the mistake is to proceed on a mistaken basis already in play. Muyun Tongmen says Shakyamuni, pressed until no route of retreat remained, could only proceed that way. Zhongfeng Mingben warns against doing so after calling each of Linji's four positions wrong. Tiebi Huiji uses the phrase for speaking despite the problem with speech, while Jieweizhou Xingzhou rejects it as an excuse for preserving a defective written account. The surrounding case therefore decides whether carrying the mistake forward is expedient, constrained, or condemned.

Senses.Explanation: "When the lead general is not bold, he drags down the whole army" makes a failed first move costly for everyone. Chan masters use the proverb to judge an inadequate response or perform the problem before their listeners. Tianan gives it after a hall respondent passes without answering; Zhangxue gives it to a monk who volunteers for a confrontation. Jiean applies it to earlier case speakers; Chaozong turns it on a worker asking about sauce. Pufu stages a fall, says the line, and asks to be helped up.

Senses.PreferredTarget: If the commander is not fierce, the whole army suffers.
AlternateTargets: A timid leader brings trouble on all three divisions of the army.
SearchAliases: weak commander troubles whole army Chan
general not fierce army suffers Zen
Senses.Note: Ruibai uses the saying after a mistimed bow; Zishui says it after striking the board before his assembly. Wujian applies it to an inherited exchange about Deshan, and Hengchuan deploys it after comparing different ways of occupying a hall. The borrowed military image presses the speaker to act decisively when an entire encounter depends on it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 者是什麼人？馬祖云：待汝一口吸盡西江水，却向汝道。士有省，師頌云：一口吸盡西江水，鷓鴣啼在深花裏，縱饒直下便承當，何啻白雲千萬里？曳拄杖，下座。小參。臨濟入門便喝、德山入門便棒，亂世英雄；雪老低頭歸菴、麻谷携鋤入園，太平奸賊。所以道：句中不停意，意中不停句，意句不同倫。且作麼生會？直饒向劍刃上翻身、氷稜上走馬，也是無風匝匝之波。不見雲門道：盡乾坤大地無絲毫過患，猶是轉句。不見一法始是半提，更須知有全提底。且作麼生是全提底？擊拂子，云：自出洞來無敵手，得饒人處且饒人。復舉：臨濟聞德山示眾云：道得也三十棒，道不得也三十棒。濟令侍者去問：為什麼道得也三十棒、道不得也三十棒？他若打你，接住送一送，看他如何？侍者至彼理前問，德山便打，侍者接住送一送，德山便歸方丈。侍者回，舉似臨濟，濟云：我從來疑著者漢。雖然如是，汝還見德山麼？侍者擬議，濟便打，師云：千鈞之弩，豈為鼷鼠發機？奔流度刃、疾燄過風則不無，二老仔細撿點將來，三十棒只合自喫。何故？將頭不猛，累及三軍。擊拂子，下座。小參小參過去諸如來，斯門已成就，夢裏求形，水中捉月。現在諸菩薩，今各入圓明浦，得老鼠打破油甕。未來修學人，當依如是法，彼自無瘡，勿傷之也。無計較中翻成計較，無途轍中翻成途轍。殊不知屠坊酒肆，全彰古佛家風；閙市紅塵，顯出祖師巴鼻。若也舉一明三，目機銖兩，何啻白雲萬里？嗄！華開華落任風吹，自有清香滿天地。復舉：雪峯示眾云：三世諸佛向火𦦨上轉大法輪。玄沙云：近日官令稍嚴。峯云：作麼生？沙云：不許攙行奪市。雪峰不覺吐舌。雲門云：火𦦨為三世諸佛說法，三世諸佛立地聽。師云：雪峰父子將謂播揚大教，殊不知馳騁機解，衒耀見聞。雲門忍俊不禁，道個火𦦨為三世諸佛說法。且道畢竟說什麼法？離婁明未徹，師曠聽非聰。便下座。白雲度參，問：西來密意未審如何？師云：待娑羅峰點頭即向汝道。度以手搖曳擬答，師便喝，度云：娑羅峰頂白浪滔天，花開芒種後，葉落立秋前。師云：我家無殘羮剩飯也。度云：此非殘羮剩飯而何？師頷之。法語法語示徐提點示徐提點信是道元功德母，長養一切諸善根。先聖曲垂方便，出一言半句，無非應病與藥，又何甞以實法繫綴於人？迷則千差萬別，悟則事同一家。葢因積劫以來，無明煩惱所覆，不能洞徹見源，豈可汩沒塵勞，虗喪光陰？一念稍有差別，墮在三惡

Occurrences.Kwic: 扇子𨁝跳上三十三天，築著帝釋鼻孔，東海鯉魚打一棒，雨似盆傾。佛誕日，上堂。哇地一聲諸境現，周行七步更多能。老僧不是多饒舌，要與諸人絕謂情。歲旦，上堂：元正啟祚，萬物咸新。是第二句，還我第一句來。天童月坡和尚遺書至，上堂：從上來，死衲子心能有幾人？活衲子眼能有幾人？昨夜玲瓏巖吞却太白峯，月坡和尚遷化去也。上堂：百千三昧門，百千神通門，百千妙用門，你總入不得。你為三昧礙，神通礙，妙用礙？直饒不礙，也入不得。月舟西堂至，上堂。千丈巖前看瀑布，即是西來祖意；鄮嶺山中把手言語，即是西來祖意。拈拄杖，云：庭前柏樹子，一夜風吹落。冬至，小參。群陰欲去未去之際，一陽欲來未來之時，樓上鐘鳴，堂前鼓響，凡聖交參，一期事畢，開口不在舌頭上。不在舌頭上，在甚麼上？瞎却天下人眼，現前一眾滴水冰生。上堂：百草頭上泄天機，閙市頭邊露真智。釋迦老子無藏身處即且置，你諸人衲衣下一句作麼生道？歸新僧堂，上堂。古人道：居此堂者，有利有害。老僧道：居此堂者，無利無害。將頭不猛，累及三軍。陳如尊者一坐坐斷，四百箇衲僧上無攀仰、下絕己躬，常光現前，壁立萬仞。拈拄杖，云：有利無利，不離行市。今年桃李貴，一顆直千金。上堂：無邊身菩薩不見如來頂相，才說無邊便有限量，爭見如來頂相？如來頂相只在諸人面前，巍巍堂堂，離一切見。解夏，上堂：長期百二十日，短期九十日。無繩自縛底有甚數？十字縱橫底有甚數？上堂：諸佛不著便，諸祖不著便。今日老僧不著便，你諸人上來也不著便。顯掌財下火，要與你顯露本有靈光。你三度為掌財來，情塵濃厚，紅爐𦦨上雪花飛。上堂：真人面前，一點伎倆用不得。九烏射盡，一翳猶存。一箭墮地，天下不黑。上堂：諸上座體取佛意，無事安樂底，便是一得永得。不同善財暫時斂念，樓閣門開。上堂。性非垢淨，湛然圓滿。諸佛菩提，眾生煩惱。驀拈拄杖擊香臺，云：針眼魚吞却嘉州大像。上堂：明暗色空，不曾礙人。一念周沙界，日用萬般通。湛然常寂寂，常轉自家風。園頭下火。園中種作不違時，是汝為頭都得知。莫謂荼毗沒分付，老僧不見一莖眉。上堂：明上座悟去，六祖與他道：什麼不思善，不思惡？正當恁麼時，那箇是明上座本來面目？若因此，老僧今日亦恁麼舉，諸人何不悟去？明上座禮拜，問曰：上來密語密意外，還更別有意否？祖曰：我與汝說者，即非密也。汝若返照自己面

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 茶話。師云：「弁山沒有甚麼與大眾分歲，有一則古語，舉似大眾。三祖云：『至道無難。惟嫌簡擇。但莫憎愛，洞然明白。』今日是除歲，明日是新年。作麼生不簡擇？左邊是廚房。右邊是齋堂。作麼生得無憎愛？若向這裏曉得親，剝泥牛與大眾分歲；其或未然。且歸堂中參究，不得草草。」僧出云：「嶺上寒梅帶雪開。」師云：「是簡擇。」進云：「多謝泥牛。」師云：「又是憎愛。」又僧云：「和尚未開口已前，早已勘破了也。」師云：「灼然簡擇。」僧便喝。師云：「憎愛。」端陽茶話。「今日端陽佳節，畫龍艾虎鬥額，奪得錦標歸來，特與諸君漏泄目。作麼生是漏泄的事？石榴紅似火，梔子白如綿。」豎碑茶話。「碑文鐫白字，萬古徽猷；當道種青松，見聞不昧。如此會得，猶在半途。如此不會，白雲萬里。會麼？」良久云：「弁山一日雨，橋流水不流。」僧問：「弁山風景事如何？」師云：「花紅柳綠。」進云：「還有向上事也無？」師云：「有。」進云：「如何是向上事？」師云：「弁山吞卻西湖月。」僧禮拜，師打云：「將頭不猛，累及三軍。」唐祈遠居士設茶。師云：「內護外護要心堅，般若通明絕萬緣，透出毘盧頂𩕳外，始是吾家祖師禪。般若無名，非凡聖故；般若無形，非長短故；般若無相，非青黃故；般若無知，非意識故。欲學般若者，將心意識掃得絜潔淨淨，然後始相應也。古云：『眾生心識，處處能緣，惟不能緣於般若之上。』蓋般若離一切相故。諸人還會得般若麼？藕斷絲不斷，功深願亦深。」普茶。師問眾云：「紹興請山僧戒珠寺開堂，且道我去？不去？若道不去，古人云：『隨緣赴感靡不周。』若道去，又道：『而恒處此菩提座。』若道得，許過戒珠；道不得，且住弁山。汝等諸人如何定當？」僧出云：「舟行岸移。」師云：「而恒處此菩提座聻？」又僧出云：「長空一片月。」師云：「隨緣赴感靡不周聻？」僧禮拜，師便打。沈居士請茶話。師云：「明月映寒潭，千波頓息樹，頭葉不動，大地風澄。直饒心境一如，光含萬象，未知有向上一竅在。且道如何是向上一竅？泥牛撞倒須彌頂，木馬嘶乾四海潮。莫有問話者麼？」有居士出，禮拜歸位，師云：「好與三十棒。」入就瑞白禪師語錄卷之四終入就瑞白禪師語錄卷之五明住天台護國寺嗣法門人寂蘊編茶話師赴蕺山請，過報國院，曹源禪者同眾居士設普茶，請茶話。師云：「三世諸佛為一大事因緣故，出現於世間，莫不使一切

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 扇子𨁝跳上三十三天，築著帝釋鼻孔，東海鯉魚打一棒，雨似盆傾。佛誕日，上堂。哇地一聲諸境現，周行七步更多能。老僧不是多饒舌，要與諸人絕謂情。歲旦，上堂：元正啟祚，萬物咸新。是第二句，還我第一句來。天童月坡和尚遺書至，上堂：從上來，死衲子心能有幾人？活衲子眼能有幾人？昨夜玲瓏巖吞却太白峯，月坡和尚遷化去也。上堂：百千三昧門，百千神通門，百千妙用門，你總入不得。你為三昧礙，神通礙，妙用礙？直饒不礙，也入不得。月舟西堂至，上堂。千丈巖前看瀑布，即是西來祖意；鄮嶺山中把手言語，即是西來祖意。拈拄杖，云：庭前柏樹子，一夜風吹落。冬至，小參。群陰欲去未去之際，一陽欲來未來之時，樓上鐘鳴，堂前鼓響，凡聖交參，一期事畢，開口不在舌頭上。不在舌頭上，在甚麼上？瞎却天下人眼，現前一眾滴水冰生。上堂：百草頭上泄天機，閙市頭邊露真智。釋迦老子無藏身處即且置，你諸人衲衣下一句作麼生道？歸新僧堂，上堂。古人道：居此堂者，有利有害。老僧道：居此堂者，無利無害。將頭不猛，累及三軍。陳如尊者一坐坐斷，四百箇衲僧上無攀仰、下絕己躬，常光現前，壁立萬仞。拈拄杖，云：有利無利，不離行市。今年桃李貴，一顆直千金。上堂：無邊身菩薩不見如來頂相，才說無邊便有限量，爭見如來頂相？如來頂相只在諸人面前，巍巍堂堂，離一切見。解夏，上堂：長期百二十日，短期九十日。無繩自縛底有甚數？十字縱橫底有甚數？上堂：諸佛不著便，諸祖不著便。今日老僧不著便，你諸人上來也不著便。顯掌財下火，要與你顯露本有靈光。你三度為掌財來，情塵濃厚，紅爐𦦨上雪花飛。上堂：真人面前，一點伎倆用不得。九烏射盡，一翳猶存。一箭墮地，天下不黑。上堂：諸上座體取佛意，無事安樂底，便是一得永得。不同善財暫時斂念，樓閣門開。上堂。性非垢淨，湛然圓滿。諸佛菩提，眾生煩惱。驀拈拄杖擊香臺，云：針眼魚吞却嘉州大像。上堂：明暗色空，不曾礙人。一念周沙界，日用萬般通。湛然常寂寂，常轉自家風。園頭下火。園中種作不違時，是汝為頭都得知。莫謂荼毗沒分付，老僧不見一莖眉。上堂：明上座悟去，六祖與他道：什麼不思善，不思惡？正當恁麼時，那箇是明上座本來面目？若因此，老僧今日亦恁麼舉，諸人何不悟去？明上座禮拜，問曰：上來密語密意外，還更別有意否？祖曰：我與汝說者，即非密也。汝若返照自己面

Senses.Explanation: A fish eye may look bright like a pearl without being one. Langshan, Guxue, Jianguan, Poshan, and Xutang use the mismatch to expose borrowed formulations, apparent insight, or deceptive substitutes for direct recognition. Poshan warns against polished Chan talk; Xutang turns the image into a critical verse on the Pang household. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

The paired gesture is to point to heaven and point to earth. The retained records place it in accounts of the newborn Buddha’s claim of being uniquely honored, and later hall addresses repeat, question, or criticize that paired gesture, often alongside Yunmen’s reported threat of a blow. The entry names the gesture and the recurrent recorded setting; it does not treat the gesture as a symbol requiring an added interpretation.

Senses.Explanation: To point east and mark west is to gesture or talk around in different directions. Linji Yixuan places the phrase in a list of the behavior of undiscerning teachers who see spirits, praise the weather, and fuss over lanterns and pillars. In an independent case commentary, Fojian Huiqin says that although Changsha points east and marks west, he resembles someone mistaking a bell for a jar. The phrase therefore marks directional display or discursive indirection; its judgment still comes from the surrounding turn.

Senses.Explanation: To point to a deer and call it a horse is to falsely identify one thing as another. Zhongfeng Mingben rejects a proposed identification of the ‘formless true person’ with this verdict. Hansong Zhicao applies it to empty talk of mystery, and Mingjue Cong includes it among conspicuous performances at the crossroads. In each use, the idiom condemns a claim that substitutes a name or display for what it purports to identify.

Senses.Explanation: To identify one thing as another by reversing plain names. Chan speakers use the old accusation as a direct verdict on false naming, distorted explanation, or misidentified conduct. Zhongfeng Mingben joins it to calling a servant a gentleman while rejecting an account of Linji’s person of no rank. Letan Hongying and Foyan Qingyuan use it while appraising inherited sayings and their own refusal to misname. Weizhou Qingman, Hansong Zhicao, and Tiantong Hua place it in balanced critical comparisons.

Senses.Explanation: A ceremonial action in hall addresses: Hanxiu Ruqian or Yuansou Xingduan raises an offering, incense, or verbally presented object and burns it in the censer before stating the person or purpose of the dedication. Hanxiu Ruqian uses the expression through repeated direct use in explicit incense-offering and dedication frames. Yuansou Xingduan independently deploys it through independent recorded-sayings use of the censer action. Baichi offers for the ruler, Neishao for Shakyamuni and Dharma continuity, and Qiran for his teacher: three distinct current liturgical deployments of the same censer action.

Senses.Explanation: “Pass a ladder to a thief” (與賊過梯) describes furnishing the means by which a thief advances. Gunan uses the verdict on Cuiyan’s and Xuedou’s handling of an exchange. Zhihai says any unchecked speech passes a ladder to a thief, then announces that he has caught the assembly together with the stolen goods. A preface stages an anonymous objection that publishing models might do this, then has its author reject that charge; Jiangshan applies the phrase to an appraisal of Deshan; Jinshan uses it against a reading of the Third Patriarch. The corpus thus records the phrase as a criticism of giving an opponent, imitator, or disputed reading its next foothold.

Senses.Explanation: Prajñātāra's prophecy makes transmission across vast China depend on descendants actually carrying it forward. Three lineage histories place the verse in Prajñātāra's instructions to Bodhidharma. Wuyi Yuanlai later cites it while arguing that exacting transmission proceeds through tested heirs rather than easy claims.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Though China is vast, there is no other road; its heirs must walk it underfoot
SearchAliases: though china is vast, there is no other road; its heirs must walk it underfoot
Senses.Note: The prophecy attributed to Prajñātāra says that China may be vast, yet the lineage needs heirs to walk its path. Tianyin cites it while resisting a fixed formula for Mazu's teaching; Baichi asks whether the ancestor foresaw the future or merely spoke by chance. Yunsou turns the couplet into a live declaration at his teaching seat. Huiyue calls on students to keep the ancestral lamp alive and uses the same lines to press their responsibility. The force is in the heirs' action, not a map of roads.

Occurrences.Kwic: 未生世界，早有此性；世界壞時，此性不壞。如何是不壞之性？州云：四大五蘊甘草甜。僧云：這箇是壞底。如何是不壞之性？州云：四大五蘊黃連苦。還知趙州老漢舌頭落處麼？盡山河大地是四大五蘊，盡山河大地是不壞之性。若未知趙州老漢舌頭落處，則四大五蘊自在一邊，不壞之性自在一邊，驢年得休歇去。拈拄杖畫一畫云：畫斷葛藤，蝦蟇𨁝跳上天，蚯蚓抹過東海。海印蘭若華嚴經會。華月窓請普說，師云：震法雷，擊法鼓，布慈雲兮灑甘露。只如法雷未震，法鼓未擊，慈雲未布，甘露未灑，還有為人道理也無？若有為人道理，何用強生節目？是故說法者無說無示，聞法者無聞無得。無說無示，真說真示；無聞無得，真聞真得。然則一時佛事既已周圓，汝等諸人如何體悉？依希似曲纔堪聽，又被風吹別調中。復云：此是月窓藏主建華嚴經會底意旨，山僧未免陞座舉揚。約山僧見處，你諸人即是毗盧遮那，毗盧遮那與你諸人無二
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi. Chushi raises the expression in his own Huayan lecture and asks whether teaching can precede the thunder.

Senses.Explanation: A compact Buddhist preaching image used as a verbal unit; it is not merely the accidental adjacency of 震 and 法雷. Feiyin Tongrong uses the expression through Feiyin Tongrong pairs 震法雷 with 擊法鼓 while describing the raising of the teaching. Dahui Zonggao independently deploys it through The anthology preserves Dahui's repeated use 即今法雷已震. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.
